newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: De Beers says reopened Zaire buying office.
newsitem.headline: De Beers says reopened Zaire buying office.

text.p: De Beers Consolidated Mines Ltd said on Monday it had reopened a diamond buying office in Zaire's diamond capital Mbuji-Mayi, which it closed earlier this year.
De Beers spokeswoman Judith Annakie said the buying office was re-opened about 10 days ago.

"We recently reopened Mbuji-Mayi," she said, adding that De Beers recently bought two shipments of production from Zaire's Societe Miniere de Bakwanga (MIBA) diamond mine which were offered for sale by tender.
"We have bought two shipments of MIBA production which were offered for tender in competition with other bidders," Annakie said.
She gave no value for the purchases.
De Beers closed its Mbuji-Mayi operation in March and its buying office in Kisangani in December last year after Laurent Kabila's rebels took control of the towns.
The AFDL rebels have said that they want to renegotiate mining contracts issued by the government of ousted President Mobutu Sese Seko, including that of De Beers.
Annakie said De Beers officials had held three formal meetings with the rebels and talks were continuing.
"We want to do business there and talks are continuing. We have actually got representation in Lubumbashi at the moment," she said.
